subsystems.name: Hydrogen cartridge
subsystems.role: stores the fuel in a swappable container, holding enough for several charges.

subsystems.name: Fuel cell stack
subsystems.role: converts hydrogen and oxygen into electricity and water.

subsystems.name: Air and water management
subsystems.role: supplies oxygen and removes product water and waste heat.

subsystems.name: Power electronics
subsystems.role: conditions the stack output to a stable voltage for charging devices.

subsystems.name: Control system
subsystems.role: monitors temperature, pressure and current, and shuts down safely if needed.

buildSteps.title: Design the stack
buildSteps.detail: Calculate the number of cells and active area needed for the target power, typically 10–50 W for a handheld charger.

buildSteps.title: Make membrane electrode assemblies
buildSteps.detail: Coat catalyst (usually platinum) onto both sides of a polymer membrane, then add gas diffusion layers.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the stack
buildSteps.detail: Layer the MEAs with bipolar plates and seals, then compress the stack between end plates.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the hydrogen cartridge
buildSteps.detail: Fill a metal hydride canister with hydrogen, or use a small high-pressure cylinder; test leak-tightness.

buildSteps.title: Integrate balance of plant
buildSteps.detail: Connect the air pump, cooling fan, water separator and power electronics to the stack.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure power output, efficiency and start-up time; tune control software for safe operation.

buildSteps.title: Package the unit
buildSteps.detail: Assemble into a handheld casing with cartridge slot, vents for air and heat, and a charging port.

buildSteps.title: Certify and produce
buildSteps.detail: Meet safety standards for hydrogen and consumer electronics, then set up cartridge refill or exchange.

prerequisites.why: the core technology is used in vehicles and stationary power, but must be miniaturised.
metal hydride canisters and small high-pressure cylinders are already used in niche products.

prerequisites.tech: Miniature air pumps and thermal management
prerequisites.why: small fans and pumps are available from electronics cooling and medical devices.
platinum and specialty polymers keep costs high; cheaper alternatives are in development.
refilling or exchanging cartridges is not yet convenient or widespread for consumers.

pathway.milestone: niche products for military, remote monitoring and expedition use
pathway.unlocks: field-proven reliability in small fuel cell systems.

pathway.milestone: consumer chargers with easy cartridge exchange and lower cost
pathway.unlocks: clean backup power for outdoor and emergency use.

pathway.milestone: green hydrogen cartridges from renewable electricity
replacing batteries in high-energy applications like drones and laptops
pathway.unlocks: longer runtime and faster refuelling than lithium batteries.
